title: move_to must convert non-ndarray containers (pandas Series, lists) to numpy before dlpack transfer
answers: classification metric fails with pandas Series y_true and torch/array_api_strict y_pred under array_api_dispatch
move_to dlpack error with pandas Series
pandas categorical labels break array API metrics on another device
mixed pandas and array API inputs to accuracy_score/f1_score
body:
Symptom: with array_api_dispatch=True, classification metrics raised errors when y_true was a pandas Series (int or categorical) and y_pred/y_prob came from another namespace or device (e.g. torch, array_api_strict device1).
Root cause: sklearn/utils/_array_api.py:move_to. get_namespace reports the numpy namespace for pandas Series and lists, but those objects do not support the dlpack protocol, so the cross-namespace transfer failed.
Fix pattern: in move_to, when the source namespace is numpy, the target is not numpy, and the object is not a numpy.ndarray, call numpy.asarray(array) before the dlpack transfer. The torch negative-stride workaround (numpy.ascontiguousarray) runs after this step, so it also applies to the converted array.
Constraints: the conversion happens only when the target namespace is not numpy. A transfer from numpy to numpy keeps the original container. Any new cross-namespace helper must also normalise array-likes to ndarray before it uses __dlpack__.
applies: sklearn/utils/_array_api.py move_to and any metric/estimator receiving pandas or list inputs alongside array API arrays
